In [[mathematics]], the '''Suita conjecture''' is a conjecture related to the theory of the [[Riemann surface]], the boundary behavior of [[conformal map]]s, the theory of [[Bergman kernel]], and the theory of the L<sup>2</sup> extension. The conjecture states the following:

{{blockquote|{{harvtxt|Suita|1972}}: Let {{math|R}} be an Riemann surface, which admits a nontrivial Green function <math>G_R</math>. Let <math>\omega</math> be a local coordinate on a neighborhood <math>V_{z_0}</math> of <math>z_0 \in R</math> satisfying <math>w(z_0) = 0</math>. Let <math>\kappa R</math> be the Bergman kernel for holomorphic (1, 0) forms on {{math|R}}. We define <math>B_{R}(z)|dw|^2 := \kappa_{R}(z)|_{V_{z_0}}</math>, and <math>B_{R}(z, \overline{t})d\omega \otimes d\overline{t} := \kappa_{R}(z,\overline{t})</math> . Let <math>c_{\beta}(z)</math> be the [[logarithmic capacity]] which is locally defined by <math>c_{\beta}(z_0) := \exp \lim_{\xi \to z} (G_{R}(z, z_{0}) -\log |\omega(z)|)</math> on {{math|R}}. Then, the inequality <math>(c_{\beta}(z_{0}))^2 \leq \pi B_{R}(z_0)</math> holds on the every open Riemann surface {{math|R}}, and also, with equality, then <math>B_{R} \equiv 0</math> or, {{math|R}} is conformally equivalent to the unit disc less a (possible) closed set of inner capacity zero.<ref>{{harvtxt|Guan|Zhou|2015}}</ref>}}

It was first proved by {{harvtxt|Błocki|2013}} for the bounded plane domain and then completely in a more generalized version by {{harvtxt|Guan|Zhou|2015}}. Also, another proof of the Suita conjecture and 
some examples of its generalization to [[several complex variables]] (the multi (high) - dimensional Suita conjecture) were given in {{harvtxt|Błocki|2014a}} and {{harvtxt|Błocki|Zwonek|2020}}. The multi (high) - dimensional Suita conjecture fails in non-[[pseudoconvex domain]]s.<ref>{{harvtxt|Nikolov|2015}}, {{harvtxt|Nikolov|Thomas|2021}}</ref> This conjecture was proved through the optimal estimation of the [[Ohsawa–Takegoshi L2 extension theorem|Ohsawa–Takegoshi ''L''<sup>2</sup> extension theorem]].
